lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Make sure the code link leads directly to a polished profile or repository list.
items.because: It should show relevant projects and documentation.

items.says: Remove the date of birth.
items.because: It does not establish qualifications and may create hiring bias.

items.says: Remove nationality unless the application requires it.
items.because: It is generally irrelevant to hiring decisions and may introduce bias.

items.says: Consider adding a relevant specialization, thesis, or courses.
items.because: They could strengthen an application for a role related to the degree.

items.says: Replace “Country” with the actual country name if it is a placeholder.
items.because: The location should be accurate before submission.

items.says: Consider adding a strong academic distinction, major project, or relevant coursework.
items.because: It may be more valuable than weaker project content if there is room.

items.says: Define what the 35% diagnostic-accuracy improvement measures.
items.because: “Accuracy” could mean several different metrics.

items.says: Identify the evaluation dataset or basis.
items.because: The reader currently has to infer how the result was evaluated.

items.says: Clarify whether interventions besides adapter fine-tuning contributed.
items.because: The bullet does not make clear what changed.

items.says: Explain the source of the “validated tool-use trajectories” or what made them validated.
items.because: The phrase may be unclear outside the team.

items.says: Define reviewer disagreement and how it was measured.
items.because: The 14% to 6% result needs a clearer metric.

items.says: Make the agents’ architecture and routing responsibility easier to understand.
items.because: “Each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer” is difficult to parse.

items.says: Say whether routing alone produced the reduction.
items.because: Prompt or model changes may also have contributed.

items.says: Explain “in-scope signals” in more general language.
items.because: It may be an internal term.

items.says: Specify what “equal accuracy” means.
items.because: It could mean statistical equivalence, an exact match, or a specified tolerance.

items.says: Define “grouped tool-use rollouts” for general ML engineering readers.
items.because: The terminology is specialized.

items.says: Say whether the tool-call and latency reductions came from a fixed test set or production.
items.because: The measurement setting is unclear.

items.says: Avoid overemphasizing GRPO terminology for roles that do not value LLM post-training.
items.because: The terminology is specialized.

items.says: Make the scope of the evaluation harness more explicit.
items.because: Test execution, metrics, reporting, checkpoint comparison, and release gating imply different ownership.

items.says: Clarify what “citation quality” measured.
items.because: The metric is not defined.

items.says: Explain whether the two regressions were blocked from release or identified during experimentation.
items.because: Their significance is unclear.

items.says: The assistant-only loss-masking technique duplicates the first internship bullet.
items.because: It is already included in the 35% improvement bullet.

items.says: Assistant-only loss masking does not necessarily train a model to reproduce tool outputs.
items.because: It generally trains on assistant-generated tokens while conditioning on other messages.

items.says: The triage and backlog accomplishment appears again in the research project.
items.because: The same result should not appear in both places.

items.says: Define “pending-case backlog” and how the eight-week comparison was calculated.
items.because: The result’s meaning and baseline are unclear.

items.says: Explain what the system did with the 800+ sensor signals.
items.because: It is unclear whether it processed, ranked, filtered, or classified them.

items.says: Avoid implying the branch alone caused the backlog reduction if operational changes contributed.
items.because: Other changes may have influenced the 68% result.

items.says: Replace “Country” with the actual country name if it is a placeholder.
items.because: The location should be accurate before submission.

items.says: Specify which GPU-memory measurement fell by 4x.
items.because: Peak allocated, reserved, and total training memory are different measures.

items.says: State whether model quality, throughput, or convergence remained unchanged, if verified.
items.because: Readers may want to know the trade-offs.

items.says: Clarify whether BF16 affected training stability.
items.because: The bullet does not address that possible trade-off.

items.says: Say whether both latency figures used the same traffic profile.
items.because: The before-and-after comparison needs a consistent basis.

items.says: Clarify whether caching and batching were both necessary or one was the primary cause.
items.because: Their respective contributions are unclear.

items.says: Fix the grammatical mismatch between “Maintained” and “adds.”
items.because: The bullet combines incompatible verb forms.

items.says: Clarify whether you maintained, redesigned, or added checks to the pipeline.
items.because: The scope of your work is unclear.

items.says: Define what “release cycles to 3 days” means.
items.because: It could describe time from change to release or a release cadence.

items.says: Specify what the regression checks covered.
items.because: They could test model quality, latency, memory, compatibility, or deployment health.

items.says: Explain and measure what removing the nightly backlogs meant operationally.
items.because: The outcome is currently qualitative.

items.says: Add measurable effects on failures, dispatch, reliability, or incidents if available.
items.because: Those would be stronger than the qualitative outcome.

items.says: Consider de-emphasizing dead-letter handling for ML-focused roles.
items.because: It may matter less outside backend, platform, or production engineering roles.

items.says: Remove or substantiate the broad adoption and outcome claims.
items.because: “AI-first,” “accelerating delivery,” and “improving outcomes” lack a measurable result.

items.says: Say what you built, what changed, and how adoption was measured.
items.because: The bullet does not provide that evidence for its leadership claim.

items.says: Define what grew 100x in the raw conversation.
items.because: It could refer to tokens, messages, or input history size.

items.says: Describe the stress test and whether compaction preserved task performance.
items.because: The 100-turn result does not establish how the test worked or what it retained.

items.says: Explain the purpose of the context layers and staged compaction.
items.because: The surrounding project description should make the concepts understandable.

items.says: Explain how you verified that deadlocks and lost results were removed.
items.because: The evidence could come from stress tests, production incidents, or both.

items.says: Define what “50-way fan-out” counts.
items.because: It could mean concurrent agents, tool calls, or requests.

items.says: Add reliability numbers, failure-rate reductions, or test duration if available.
items.because: They would make the result more persuasive.

items.says: Identify the framework or link to the implementation if it is publicly visible.
items.because: Readers could then verify the project and work.

items.says: Name the general categories of the eight metrics.
items.because: “Citation and faithfulness metrics” gives little detail about them.

items.says: Clarify whether you designed the integrations, implemented existing definitions, or worked as part of a team.
items.because: Your precise contribution is unclear.

items.says: Use a more specific role than “Contributor” if you owned the module changes.
items.because: “Contributor” may undersell your responsibility.

items.says: Specify what the Kendall correlation compares.
items.because: The reference could be degradation levels, human judgments, or something else.

items.says: Define injected degradation and what the 400+ trials represent.
items.because: The trials could be independent reports, perturbations, or evaluation runs.

items.says: Include statistical significance, confidence intervals, or degradation range if measured.
items.because: They would provide more context for the result.

items.says: The backlog result duplicates the Mobility Systems internship bullet.
items.because: It may look as though the same result was counted twice.

items.says: Remove the industrial-diagnostics result from the research-agent project.
items.because: It creates uncertainty about project boundaries and ownership.

items.says: Expand the programming skills list with relevant, demonstrated capabilities.
items.because: It is too short relative to the experience shown.

items.says: Consider replacing Git if space is limited.
items.because: A demonstrated engineering capability may be more valuable than a basic tool.

items.says: Broaden the narrow ML and agents skills list with relevant, demonstrated technologies.
items.because: The experience shows capabilities not represented here.

items.says: Separate frameworks and libraries from methods or areas of expertise.
items.because: Readers should be able to distinguish tools from concepts.

items.says: Specify the types of “agent evaluation” performed.
items.because: The phrase is broad.

items.says: Make the degree, internship, and project dates accurate and explainable.
items.because: The degree overlaps with the internship and projects, so recruiters may check the timeline.

items.says: Use actual country names consistently across locations.
items.because: Entries mix “Metro City, USA” with “Metro City, Country.”

items.says: Make each project’s context and ownership unmistakable.
items.because: The résumé mixes industrial diagnostics, robotics, and research-agent work without always explaining their relationship.

items.says: Use consistent bullet punctuation and formatting, without awkward manual hyphenation.
items.because: Words such as “dead-letter” should not split awkwardly.

items.says: Consider ordering projects by relevance rather than only by date.
items.because: The most relevant project depends on the target role.
